group: base-6 digit rounds (5n/2 on even blocks), Collatz-like
title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RF1RB_1LE0RA_0LB0LE_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RF1RB_1LE0RA_0LB0LE_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; it is now a question about one explicit map. The complete round map on lists of blocks is written down (py/roundmap.py) and agrees with direct simulation on more than 15,000 random block lists; it is computed, not yet a Lean theorem as a whole. Lean's kernel proves the even rounds (E n → E (5n/2 + 1)), the odd sweep (six 1s off the block, one onto the next), the top-level ends, and that the machine reaches E 26041. Iterating the map from blank tape gives no halt in 1,000,000 rounds (the block then has about 205,000 digits); a halt needs a number on the orbit to be a base-6 repunit or the like, which is astronomically unlikely but not excluded.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 34,257 cells have been visited and 32,343 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.46).

claims.title: Every even round, in closed form
claims.text: For every p: from E (2p+4) = B> 0 0 1^(2p+4) the machine reaches E (5p+11), that is n ↦ 5n/2 + 1. Built from 4 symbolic rules (entry, a sweep, two ends) and an induction on the sweeps.

claims.title: From blank tape to E 26041
claims.text: The machine reaches E 26041 through E 2, 6, 16, 41, (36, 7), 106, 266, 666, 1666, 4166, 10416: eight even rounds and three concrete runs.

claims.title: The odd sweep and the top-level ends
claims.text: With the phase state P(i, x, R) = w^i C> 0 1 0 1^x 0 R, w = 10101: for odd x ≥ 7 one sweep takes six 1s off the block, writes a w and adds one to the next block (or makes a new block), for any tape on both sides. At top level, x = 2 with nothing after ends the round in 5i + 6 ones, x = 3 in one block 5i + 6 + y, x = 5 in blocks 5i + 6 and y + 1, and x = 1 with nothing after reaches the halting transition.

claims.title: The complete round map
claims.text: A round is a recursion on phase states: odd blocks are divided by 6 by the odd sweep; an even block first runs a nested round on the blocks to its right and merges the result (with nothing to its right this is x → x − 2, so n ↦ 5n/2 + 1); the remainders 0, 1, 3, 5 end the round, differently at top level and nested (table in the README). A round halts only at top level with remainder 1 and nothing after, or nested with remainder 5 and nothing after. Compared with direct simulation on more than 15,000 random lists of up to six blocks (blocks up to 3000) with no mismatch; for one block it is the earlier table (n = 6^j·m + (6^j − 1)/5: repunits halt, even m gives n + 3m/2 + 1 + j, m ≡ 3 gives n + 3 + j, m = 6q + 5 gives (n − q + 1 + j, q + 1)), checked for every n < 200,000 against the map.

claims.title: No halt to E 326796
claims.text: Direct simulation of the rounds from blank tape: … E 26041, 32553, 32556, 81391, (79133, 2261), (65946, 15450), 130718, 326796, reached at step 34,276,754,745. The round map gives the same orbit.

claims.title: No halt in 1,000,000 rounds of the map
claims.text: The round map iterated from blank tape with big integers: 1,000,000 rounds without a halt. The tape never has more than two blocks (a round on at most two blocks ends with at most two), about 23% of the rounds start with two, and after 1,000,000 rounds the first block has about 205,000 decimal digits. This rests on the computed map.

claims.title: Why a halt is unlikely
claims.text: A round halts only when a digit recursion ends exactly: the block, after stripping trailing base-6 digits 1, must be 0 (a repunit), or in a nested round the quotients after digits 5 must come down to 0. For numbers of D base-6 digits that has chance about 6−D; second blocks are quotients of the first by a small power of 6, so they are long too. Summed over the rounds after the computed ones this is astronomically small. Small tapes do halt: (a, 5), (a, 41), (a, 257) for even a ≥ 4, and E 7, E 43, E 259.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts exactly when the orbit of (2) under the round map reaches a halting round (given the computed map). What is missing: the nested rules as Lean theorems and the reduction stated in Lean; and an argument that the orbit avoids the halting numbers, which is a Collatz-like question.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but the question is now about one explicit map. Each round works on one or two blocks of 1s: an even block grows by a factor 5/2, an odd block is divided by 6 digit by digit, and the machine stops only if such a division ends exactly. The map has been iterated for 1,000,000 rounds from blank tape without stopping.

facts.text: Every even round, proved in Lean; so are the odd sweep and the top-level ends.
Of the computed round map from blank tape, no halt; the block has about 205,000 digits.
A halt needs a base-6 repunit-like number on the orbit: very unlikely, not excluded.

sections.heading: Blocks of ones, read in rounds
html: Every round starts with the head in state B at the left end of the tape, followed by one block of 1s or two:

For an even block the head sweeps between the two ends; each sweep takes two 1s off the block and writes a 10101 on the left, and the last sweep fills those words to 1s. So E (2p+4) becomes E (5p+11): the block grows by a factor 5/2. A round costs about n² steps, so the tape grows like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: Base 6, digit by digit, with nested rounds
html: One step into a round the tape is w^i C> 0 1 0 1^x 0 R with w = 10101, i = 0, x the first block and R the other blocks. Each w becomes five 1s at the end of the round.

• Odd x ≥ 7 (Lean): a sweep takes six 1s off the block, writes a w and adds one to the next block. So the block is divided by 6: the quotient goes to the next block, the remainder 1, 3 or 5 stays.
  • Even x: the machine first runs a whole nested round on the blocks to the right and merges its result into the block; with nothing to the right the sweep is just x → x − 2 and a new w, which gives n ↦ 5n/2 + 1 (Lean).
  • Remainders end the round. At top level: 3 merges everything into one block 5i + 6 + y, 5 leaves two blocks (5i + 6, y + 1) (both Lean), and 1 starts a new round on the quotient and adds 5i + 2 to its result; if there is no quotient the machine halts (Lean). In a nested round the roles are shifted: 1 merges, 3 leaves a block, and 5 recurses on the quotient minus one, halting if there is none.
For one block this is the table

m in n = 6^j·m + (6^j − 1)/5, m ≢ 1 (mod 6)next
0 (n = 1, 7, 43, 259, …)halts
even, > 0E (n + 3m/2 + 1 + j)
≡ 3 (mod 6)E (n + 3 + j)
6q + 5(n − q + 1 + j, q + 1)

Worked example, (36, 7): 36 is even, so the 7 is run as a nested round: one odd sweep leaves remainder 1 with quotient 1, which merges to 5 + 1 = 6. The block becomes 36 − 2 + 6 = 40 with one w; twenty even sweeps later there are 21 ws and nothing left, and the round ends in 5·21 + 1 = 106 ones.
The map as a whole is computed (py/roundmap.py): it agrees with direct simulation on more than 15,000 random lists of up to six blocks.

sections.heading: Not in a million rounds
html: Lean proves the orbit up to E 26041; direct simulation reaches E 326796 after 34,276,754,745 steps; the map has been iterated for 1,000,000 rounds, where the block has about 205,000 digits. The tape never has more than two blocks.

To halt, the orbit has to meet a number whose base-6 digits end the recursion exactly, such as a repunit 11…1. For a number of D digits the chance is about 6−D, so a halt is astronomically unlikely, but excluding it means controlling the base-6 digits of a 5/2-type orbit, a Collatz-like problem nobody knows how to solve.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.46).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,257 cells (26 left of the start, 32,530 right), with a density of 1s of 0.944.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Rounds on one or two blocks of 1s by a recursive base-6 digit map, now complete (computed; the odd sweep, the even rounds and the top-level ends are Lean theorems): even n ↦ 5n/2 + 1, odd blocks are divided by 6, a round halts only when a digit recursion ends exactly; no halt in 1,000,000 rounds of the map.
